reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-level context, the full local StructureDefinition report, the deterministic aggregate as prior context, and the R4/R6 PaymentReconciliation StructureDefinitions. Direct behavior findings for PaymentReconciliation were absent; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context under the review rules.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 FMM 2/trial-use creates neutral formal stability pressure: it permits more cleanup than mature/normative content, but it does not erase the practical business impact of breaking required payment date, payment amount, and allocation detail data.

overall.oneLineConclusion: PaymentReconciliation keeps its identity but needs a resource-specific R4-to-R6 transform; avoidable naming/path breaks still have high preservation value.

reasoning.thesisMd: PaymentReconciliation is not removed or replaced, but R6 changes the root payment shape enough that a resource-level migration program is unavoidable for real R4 instances. The key drivers are the new required root `type`, required `paymentDate` to `date`, required `paymentAmount` to optional `amount`, and `detail[]` to `allocation[]` with richer targeting. Because several of these are low-cost naming or path choices rather than necessary semantic remodels, the existence of a migration program should not be treated as permission to ignore further compatibility preservation.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The actual shape is a moderate targeted remodel. Stable portions such as resource identity, status, created, period, issuer/requestor concepts, outcome path, and process notes remain recognizable. However, every R4 instance needs at least required-field renames and a synthesized root `type`; any instance with `detail[]` needs a backbone rename plus rules for `type`, request/response, and new allocation fields. The root `type` derivation can require human or business policy when R4 has no details or mixed detail categories, so the migration is not purely mechanical.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Compatibility leverage remains meaningful. A transform is needed, but retaining old wire names or paths where semantics are unchanged would avoid breaking generated APIs, FHIRPath, profiles, validation fixtures, and raw JSON for the most common required elements. This is not a `migration-program-dominates` case because the resource identity is stable and several high-impact breaks appear avoidable or preservable at modest standards cost.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest low-cost alternatives are: keep `paymentDate` rather than rename it to `date`; keep `paymentAmount` while relaxing its cardinality if optionality is desired; keep the `detail[]` backbone and add the R6 allocation children under it; and make root `type` optional or profile-required while retaining line-level category semantics. The request/response target narrowing also has less-breaking options, but those materially weaken R6's computable payment-target model or create duplicate linkage paths, so it is more plausibly a local migration chore once the allocation remodel is accepted.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinitions, SearchParameters, or HTTP behavior findings were assigned to PaymentReconciliation. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings may affect implementers' overall R6 platform migration, but under the supplied calibration they are context only and do not drive this resource-level conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The independent conclusion broadly agrees with the deterministic aggregate's Partial/moderate-targeted-remodel/preserve-where-low-cost result. The important nuance is that a PaymentReconciliation-specific migration transform is already unavoidable for ordinary instances, but that does not lower preservation value for simple required-field and backbone renames.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Structural confidence is high because the local R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions directly show the deltas. Remaining uncertainty is around official migration intent, ConceptMaps/StructureMaps, terminology aliasing, and the real-world prevalence of no-detail, mixed-detail-type, or broad out-of-set request/response references.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds mandatory root PaymentReconciliation.type
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the main non-mechanical break. R4 had required category only per `detail.type`, while R6 requires a root `type`; no-detail or mixed-detail R4 data cannot always supply that value safely. A less-breaking base design could have made root `type` optional or profile-required during transition.

findingConsiderations.title: Required paymentDate was renamed to required date
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The same required date concept changed only its wire name. Because every valid R4 instance has `paymentDate`, this forces a transform and generated API/FHIRPath churn that could largely have been avoided by retaining the old name.

findingConsiderations.title: Required paymentAmount was renamed to optional amount
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The total payment amount is central financial data. Optionality may be a legitimate R6 change, but the rename is separable and avoidable; keeping `paymentAmount` while relaxing cardinality would preserve forward compatibility for present amounts.

findingConsiderations.title: The detail backbone was renamed and expanded as allocation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `detail[]` to `allocation[]` is a broad path-level break affecting raw instances, generated models, profiles, and FHIRPath. The richer R6 children could have been added under the existing backbone path, making this a standards-review-worthy low-cost preservation opportunity.

findingConsiderations.title: Allocation request/response references changed from broad Resource targets to narrower payment targets
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can reject R4 references outside the R6 target lists and requires semantic review, but the R4 `Reference(Resource)` shape was very broad. The R6 narrowing has a credible computability rationale, so it is mainly a local migration policy item rather than a reason to change the resource-level conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: Outcome required binding changed from remittance-outcome to payment-outcome
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The path, type, cardinality, and inspected lexical codes remain stable. Terminology aliases or ConceptMaps would help tooling, but this does not materially drive R4-to-R6 instance migration.

findingConsiderations.title: paymentIssuer can now reference Patient or RelatedPerson in addition to Organization
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a forward-compatible widening: existing R4 Organization issuers remain valid. The issue is only R6-to-R4 down-conversion or local Organization-only assumptions.

findingConsiderations.title: processNote.text changed from string to markdown
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The wire shape remains an optional JSON string at the same path. Implementers should regenerate types and review rendering/sanitization behavior, but this is not a material base migration break.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional payment-source, instrument, note, and allocation fields with no native R4 representation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: These optional additions do not break R4-to-R6 validation, but they do require explicit R6-to-R4 policy for extensions, sidecar storage, or acceptable loss. They are migration chores rather than avoidable R4 compatibility breaks.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource-level behavior can affect platform migration and validators used with PaymentReconciliation, but it is not a PaymentReconciliation-specific behavior finding and is not counted toward the resource model judgment.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared search-parameter metadata issue is relevant to general R6 search infrastructure only. It does not alter the PaymentReconciliation-specific StructureDefinition migration shape.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit low-cost preservation for the unchanged required concepts: retain `paymentDate`, retain `paymentAmount` while relaxing cardinality if needed, and retain `detail[]` as the allocation backbone or provide equivalent base aliases/deprecation support.

Define an official R4-to-R6 migration map for PaymentReconciliation covering root `type` derivation, no-detail and mixed-detail category cases, required field renames, `detail[]` to `allocation[]`, and out-of-set request/response references.

Treat the narrowed allocation target model as acceptable only with clear guidance for preserving or rejecting R4 broad `Reference(Resource)` links that do not fit Claim, Account, Invoice, Encounter, Contract, or ClaimResponse.
Publish terminology aliasing or ConceptMap guidance for `remittance-outcome` to `payment-outcome`, and document R6-to-R4 handling for optional R6-only payment instrument and process-note fields.

caveats: This review is based on the local R4 4.0.1 and R6 6.0.0-ballot4 package definitions and supplied reports, not on external ballot discussion or official migration maps.
No direct behavior findings were found for PaymentReconciliation; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior is context only by instruction.
Real-world prevalence of PaymentReconciliation instances, mixed detail categories, and broad request/response target usage was not measured.
